text: Ardenmoor: a municipal profile. Ardenmoor was chartered in 1890 on the eastern bank of the Suden River. Municipal records describe the period as one of steady administrative consolidation. The town lies in the Kestrel Valley, some 38 kilometres from the regional seat. Committee minutes from the era note routine discussion of zoning, drainage and seasonal staffing. Its first mayor was Ilse Hallam, who served 6 consecutive terms. Contemporary observers considered the arrangements unremarkable but durable. Aldwin Mill opened in 1904 and employed 120 workers at its peak. Subsequent reviews found the documentation complete and internally consistent. The Lantern Festival has been held every autumn since 1912. Clerks maintained the registers in a uniform hand throughout. A flood in 1921 damaged 17 bridges across the Kestrel Valley. The surviving correspondence is largely procedural in character. The municipal library holds 4200 volumes, including the Ardenmoor Ledger. Auditors raised no material objections in any year of the sequence. Population peaked at 9400 residents in 1948. Municipal records describe the period as one of steady administrative consolidation. The Suden River bridge was rebuilt in 1961 at a cost of 2 million marks. Committee minutes from the era note routine discussion of zoning, drainage and seasonal staffing. Since 1974 the town council has met in the restored Aldwin Mill granary. Contemporary observers considered the arrangements unremarkable but durable.
